tools.name: pando_accept_proposal
tools.description: Accept what Pando worked out and pin it as the app's setup, optionally setting environment variables and secrets in the same step. This does not deploy — call pando_deploy after. On an app that is already configured it is refused unless `confirm` is true: accepting again replaces how the app is built and what it runs with what detection found, and carries over variables, how each dependency is filled, and storage. pando_get_detection_diff shows what would change. To change only a variable on a configured app, write a spec revision with pando_create_spec instead.

confirm.description: true to accept over an app that is already configured.

hostname.description: The address to serve the app at, where its routing gives it a hostname of its own.

optional.description: Dependencies the app runs without, by their keys.

secrets.description: Secret variables to set, name to value. Stored by the secrets adapter; needs app.secrets.write.

values.description: Environment variables to set, name to value, e.g. {"API_URL": "https://api"}. Stored as ordinary variables, not secrets.

tools.name: pando_add_app_to_section
tools.description: Move an app you can open into one of your launcher sections, out of any other.

tools.name: pando_ai_ask_reference
tools.description: Ask how to do something with Pando. Answered from Pando's API, CLI and MCP reference, citing the endpoints, commands and tools it relies on. Describes; does nothing.

tools.name: pando_ai_draft_access
tools.description: Draft a custom role and a group from a description of who should be able to do what. A draft only: nothing is created. Verbs come from Pando's catalog; anything else is listed as refused.

description.description: Who should be able to do what, in a sentence or two.

tools.name: pando_ai_draft_host_rules
tools.description: Propose changes to the installation's host policy from a description: the document as it would be saved, and each change. Nothing is saved. Settings fixed in the startup configuration are declined, naming where they are set.

description.description: What the rules should be, in a sentence or two.

tools.name: pando_ai_search_audit
tools.description: Ask a question of the audit log, such as "which apps did Ben Meeker create last month?". Returns a short summary and the filters used, which pando_list_audit takes as-is.

tools.name: pando_answer_detection
tools.description: Answer one of the questions from pando_get_detection. An answer that changes what is built (a build argument) has Pando build and scan the image again, so the plan shows the score of what will run: detection reads as `running` until it has, and accepting waits for it.

tools.name: pando_approve_deploy
tools.description: Approve a deploy that is waiting for approval. When it is the last approval the deploy needs, the deploy starts. Approval is a person's sign-off, so by default an installation does not let an agent's token approve; the refusal says so.

comment.description: Optional. A note recorded with the approval.

deployment_id.description: The deploy's ID, as pando_list_approvals or pando_deploy returned it.

tools.name: pando_assign_ai_function
tools.description: Have an AI adapter handle one AI function, optionally on a model of its own. Refused while another adapter handles the function; unassign it there first.

adapter_id.description: The AI adapter's ID, such as ai_anthropic.

function.description: The AI function, such as search_audit. pando_list_ai_functions lists them.

model.description: A model for this function only. Omit to use the adapter's own.

tools.name: pando_authorize_source
tools.description: Start signing a source connection in. By device code (the default) it returns user_code and verification_url: tell the person to open the URL and enter the code, then call pando_poll_source_authorization every interval_seconds until it says authorized. A connection whose capabilities have web_authorization and not device_authorization — a GitHub App, which Pando creates on GitHub and then installs — takes mode web: give the person authorize_url to open in a browser signed in to Pando, and check pando_list_sources afterwards.

tools.name: pando_check_app_image
tools.description: For an app deployed from a published image: whether its tag, such as :latest, now names a different build than the one the app runs. Writes nothing. When `update_available` is true, pando_deploy_newer_image with `latest_digest` deploys that build.

tools.name: pando_check_updates
tools.description: Ask GitHub for Pando's releases now rather than waiting for the six-hourly check, and answer as pando_get_updates does. A second request within a minute answers from the first. Sends nothing while host policy's disable_update_check is set.

tools.name: pando_clear_app_icon
tools.description: Remove the image on an app's launcher tile, so the tile shows the map generated for it.

tools.name: pando_configure_adapter
tools.description: Add an adapter, or change one by its id. Settings go in config; a secret such as an API key or a registry password goes in credentials, which is stored encrypted and never shown again. A source connection or an image registry is used from the moment it is saved; any other adapter after Pando restarts. enabled: false turns one off.

category.description: The category, such as image_registry, as pando_list_adapter_kinds lists it.

credentials.description: The kind's secret settings, by key. A key sent empty removes that credential.

enabled.description: false turns it off. Left out, it is on.

id.description: The adapter's id, such as reg_main. An existing id changes that adapter.

is_default.description: Make it the default in its category, in place of the current default. The result's replaced_default names that adapter and handover says what changes; tell the person both.

kind.description: The kind within the category, such as oci or ecr.

name.description: A name for people to read.

tools.name: pando_connect_notify
tools.description: Connect a notification adapter such as Slack to its provider. mode web takes token, a Slack configuration token (Slack's app settings, Your App Configuration Tokens, Generate Token) used once and never stored; Pando creates its app and returns authorize_url for the person to open in a browser signed in to Pando and choose Allow. Slack returns only to an https address. mode manual without token returns authorize_url, which creates the app in Slack by hand; with token, the bot token it shows once installed, it finishes. Check pando_list_notify_adapters afterwards.

token.description: For web, a Slack configuration token; for manual, the app's bot token, or omit for the link.

tools.name: pando_count_unread_notifications
tools.description: How many of your notifications are unread, without listing them.

tools.name: pando_create_app
tools.description: Create an app from a git repository (source_url), from an image that is already built (image), or from files you will send next (upload: true, then pando_upload_source). Give exactly one. Returns immediately with the app in draft while Pando works out how to run it; call pando_get_detection next, with wait_seconds to wait for it to finish. For an upload, detection starts when pando_upload_source is followed by pando_rerun_detection.

connection.description: Optional, with source_url: the source connection (from pando_list_sources) to read a private repository with. Left out, the one covering the URL is used.

image.description: An image reference such as ghcr.io/acme/web:1.4, run as it is.

name.description: A short name for the app.

ref.description: Branch or tag. Optional, with source_url.

registry_credential.description: Optional, with image: the credential a private image is pulled with. Either kind basic with username and password (a token that can read the image), or kind ecr with access_key_id, secret_access_key and optionally region, for AWS ECR.

access_key_id.description: With ecr: the AWS access key ID.

password.description: With basic: the password or access token.

region.description: With ecr: the region. Optional; read from the registry host.

secret_access_key.description: With ecr: the AWS secret access key.

upload.description: True to create the app for files sent with pando_upload_source.

tools.name: pando_create_join_token
tools.description: Create a token a new Pando joins this installation with, at its setup. `join` in the reply is the token and is shown once. A token for the control role needs every install permission.

address.description: The installation's address the joining host reaches, such as https://pando.example.com. Left out, this server's advertise address.

expires_hours.description: How many hours it lasts. Left out, 24.

max_uses.description: How many hosts may join with it. Left out, 1.

roles.description: control, app, or both. Left out: both while the cluster has fewer than three hosts, then app.

tools.name: pando_create_section
tools.description: Make a section in your own launcher: a named grouping of apps. Only you see it.

tools.name: pando_create_spec
tools.description: Write a new spec revision: the way to change a configured app's variables, egress, workloads or anything else in its spec. Send the whole spec — read the pinned one with pando_get_spec, change it, and send it back. Revisions are append-only, and this neither pins nor deploys: call pando_pin_spec with the revision it returns, then pando_deploy. With `dry_run` true nothing is written; the reply says whether the spec is accepted, the egress rules it would run with, and whether deploying it would need approval.

dry_run.description: true to check the spec without writing it.

spec.description: The whole spec, as pando_get_spec returns it under `body`.

tools.name: pando_create_subscription
tools.description: Subscribe to events and send them to a webhook (url) or through a notification adapter such as Slack or email (adapter_id). events is a comma-separated list of event names, prefixes such as deploy.*, or *; pando_list_events lists them. With app_id it is about one app; without, it is install-wide and needs install.events.manage. A webhook's signing key is in the result once; tell the person to keep it.

adapter_id.description: A notification adapter's ID. Give this or url.

channel.description: The channel it posts to, for an adapter whose destination says channels, such as Slack; pando_list_notify_channels lists them.

content_type.description: A webhook's content type. Optional; application/json by default.

description.description: What the subscription is for. Optional.

events.description: Comma-separated event names or patterns, such as deploy.failed,app.state_changed.

headers.description: A webhook's own headers, one "Name: value" per line, such as an Authorization its receiver needs. Optional.

method.description: A webhook's HTTP method: POST, PUT or PATCH. Optional.

payload_template.description: A webhook's body as a Go template, such as {"text": {{json .Subject}}}. Optional; Pando's envelope by default.

url.description: The webhook URL to post to. Give this or adapter_id.

tools.name: pando_delete_secret
tools.description: Remove one of an app's secrets. Needs app.secrets.write.

tools.name: pando_delete_section
tools.description: Delete one of your launcher sections. Its apps go back to Your apps; nothing else changes.

tools.name: pando_delete_subscription
tools.description: Delete a subscription, its signing key and its delivery log.

tools.name: pando_deploy
tools.description: Deploy an app. Returns once the deployment has been accepted, not once it is running. Without `spec_revision` it ships the pinned revision; an edit, from the console or pando_create_spec, writes a newer one, and the reply's `newer_revision` names it — deploy again with that revision to ship the edit. When the deploy needs somebody's approval, it comes back with status `awaiting_approval` and `approval_reasons` saying why; it runs once a person approves it.

idempotency_key.description: A key you choose. Retrying with the same key will not deploy twice.

spec_revision.description: The revision to deploy, by number, such as the newest from pando_list_specs. Left out, the pinned one.

tools.name: pando_deploy_newer_image
tools.description: Deploy the newer build pando_check_app_image found: writes a revision pinning `digest` and deploys it. Refused if the tag has moved since the check; check again then. Answers as pando_deploy does, approval included.

tools.name: pando_diff_specs
tools.description: Compare two spec revisions: what changed, and whether deploying it restarts, rebuilds or leaves the app alone.

from.description: The earlier revision, by number or ID.

to.description: The later revision, by number or ID.

tools.name: pando_edit_role
tools.description: Rename a custom role, replace its permissions, or both. The verbs must be of the role's scope; built-in roles cannot be changed. Changing an installation role needs every installation permission it carries before and after; permissions added to an app role must be yours on every app it is granted on. Needs install.users.manage.

name.description: The new name. Leave out to keep it.

verbs.description: Every permission the role carries, from the verb catalog. Leave out to keep them.

tools.name: pando_favorite_app
tools.description: Pin an app to the top of your own launcher. It grants nothing and only you see it; you must be able to open the app.

tools.name: pando_get_address
tools.description: Where an app is reached: its routing (adapter, mode, hostname, path or port) and address, next_address when a change is saved and not yet deployed, and the routing adapters it could move to — each with the modes it serves, its default mode, base_domain, and domains: every domain a hostname can be in, such as each of a Cloudflare adapter's zones.

tools.name: pando_get_app
tools.description: Get one app: its name, source, state and pinned spec. Once the app has been through detection, `detection` says where that has got to — `status`, and `stage` while it is running — which is why an app in draft is still in draft.

tools.name: pando_get_app_idle
tools.description: When Pando stops or deletes an app nobody uses: the app's own stop_days and delete_days (null is the installation's, 0 is never), the installation's, the ones in force, last_activity_at, stops_at and deletes_at if nobody uses it before then, and stopped_for_idle when Pando stopped it.

tools.name: pando_get_app_limit
tools.description: How many apps a person may own. With user_id: the limit in force (0 is unlimited), where it comes from (user, group or policy, with the group's name), how many apps they own, and the value on their own account. With group_id: the group's max_apps, null when it sets none. Your own account needs no permission; anything else needs install.users.manage.

group_id.description: A group's ID. Give this or user_id.

user_id.description: An account's ID. Give this or group_id.

tools.name: pando_get_auto_deploy
tools.description: Whether an app deploys automatically when its repository changes, and how: `settings` on the newest configuration and `deployed` on the running one, with `pending` when they differ; `paused` when approval now stops it; `last_check`, what Pando last found and the last commit it tried (each commit is tried once) and why it went nowhere; and the webhook URL, with whether a webhook secret is set.

tools.name: pando_get_config
tools.description: The configuration the Pando server started with: every non-secret setting, its value and where it was set (an environment variable, the config file, or the default), and the host policy fields fixed there, which cannot be changed through the API while they are set.

tools.name: pando_get_delivery
tools.description: One delivery: every attempt at it, with the status code and error each got, and the payload sent.

tools.name: pando_get_detection
tools.description: What Pando worked out about an app, including any questions it needs answered before it can deploy. The questions are written to be answerable by whatever wrote the app. `status` is `running` while Pando is still working: call again. While running, `stage` says what it is doing — fetching (cloning the repository), detecting (working out what the app is), building (building the image the app would run, so the plan can show its security score), trying (a trial run), scanning (a security scan) or screening (an AI adapter checking the plan); `running` lists every step under way, since the scan runs beside the build and the trial; and `elapsed_seconds` says how long it has taken so far; a build or a trial run can take several minutes. Pass wait_seconds (up to 60) to have the call return as soon as the stage changes or detection finishes, instead of calling repeatedly. When it has finished, `status` is ready (call pando_accept_proposal), needs_answers or unknown (answer the questions with pando_answer_detection), blocked or failed (the `detection` field says why).

wait_seconds.description: Optional. While detection is running, wait up to this many seconds (at most 60) for it to move on before answering. 0 or absent answers at once.

tools.name: pando_get_detection_diff
tools.description: What accepting the proposal would change about the app's pinned configuration: each change with its class (benign, restart, rebuild or destructive) and a summary. `is_first` is true when the app is not configured yet, so everything is new.

tools.name: pando_get_last_upgrade
tools.description: The most recent in-place upgrade of Pando: from and to which version, whether it succeeded or was rolled back and why, with the new version's last log lines when it was.

tools.name: pando_get_logs
tools.description: Read an app's recent logs. An app can be made of several parts — a web service, a worker, a database it brought with it — and each has its own log. Without `workload` this is the primary part, the one the app's address resolves to; pando_get_status lists the names. Returns the most recent lines: 200 unless `tail` says otherwise, and never more than 5000.

tail.description: Optional. How many of the most recent lines to return, 1 to 5000. Defaults to 200.

workload.description: Which part of the app to read. Defaults to the primary one.

tools.name: pando_get_notification_preferences
tools.description: Which of Pando's own notifications reach you, on each channel that reaches people, such as the console and email.

tools.name: pando_get_registry_credential
tools.description: Whether an image app has a registry credential, and of which kind, with its username or access key ID. Never the password or secret key.

tools.name: pando_get_spec
tools.description: Read one spec revision in full: how the app is built, what it runs, its variables, egress and routing.

revision.description: The revision number, such as "3", or the revision's ID.

tools.name: pando_get_status
tools.description: What an app is doing right now: running, degraded, failed, and why — including each part separately, so a single part that is crash-looping is visible rather than averaged into one word for the app.

tools.name: pando_get_two_factor
tools.description: Who you are (GET /me), including, on a local account, two_factor: whether two-factor authentication is on, whether host policy requires it, and how many recovery codes are left. Setting it up or changing it is done in the console's settings or with `pando two-factor`, never here: each step handles an authenticator key, recovery codes or your password.

tools.name: pando_get_updates
tools.description: Whether a newer Pando is released: the version the server runs, the latest on the update channel, and each version in between with its changelog, security fixes and breaking changes marked, plus the command that upgrades the server. The check is host policy (disable_update_check, update_channel).

tools.name: pando_get_usage
tools.description: What each part of an app is using right now: CPU (thousandths of a core), memory and disk in bytes, and each mounted volume's size, beside its limits (0 means none). A reading, not a history.

tools.name: pando_get_user
tools.description: One account, with every installation role it holds and where each comes from (install_roles), as pando_list_users shows it. Your own needs no permission; anyone else's needs install.view.

tools.name: pando_ignore_notice
tools.description: Hide one of an app's notices from yourself until what it says changes. Only you: everyone else still sees it. It hides a reminder and nothing more — a deploy the notice warned about is still refused.

key.description: The notice's key, as pando_list_notices lists it, such as variables.unset.

tools.name: pando_list_adapter_kinds
tools.description: The kinds of adapter this build of Pando can run, and the settings each takes: which are credentials, which are required, and the default each takes when left out.

tools.name: pando_list_adapters
tools.description: The adapters this installation is configured with — runtimes, routing, builders, image registries, secrets, backup, scanners, AI, source connections and the rest — each with its live capabilities, whether it is reachable, which credentials are set (never their values), and whether it waits on a restart. One declared at startup is read-only.

tools.name: pando_list_ai_functions
tools.description: Each AI function Pando has, the AI adapter that handles it and on which model, whether it is on, and whether the startup configuration assigns it.

tools.name: pando_list_app_events
tools.description: An app's recent events, newest first: deploys, state and health changes, scans, shares, backups. Each says what happened in a sentence.

tools.name: pando_list_approvals
tools.description: List the deploys waiting for approval on every app you can see. Each says which app, why it needs approval, the approvals it has so far, and `can_decide`: whether you may approve or reject it. Oldest first, a page at a time: pass `next_cursor` back as `cursor` for the next page.

cursor.description: The next_cursor from a previous page.

decidable.description: true to list only the deploys you may approve or reject.

tools.name: pando_list_apps
tools.description: List the apps you can manage, with their current state, newest first, a page at a time. Each app has its `address`, its owner's name (`owner_name`), and `access`, who can open it: `private` (its owner alone), `shared` (its owner and the people or groups it is shared with), `public` (anyone on the internet, without signing in) or `passcode` (anyone on the internet who has the passcode). `notice_count` is how many of its notices you have not ignored (pando_list_notices lists them), left out when none. `total` is how many match; pass `next_cursor` back as `cursor` for the next page.

cursor.description: The next_cursor from a previous page.

q.description: Only apps whose name or slug contains this.

tools.name: pando_list_audit
tools.description: Read the audit log, newest first. Every filter is optional and they combine: what was done (an action prefix such as app. or grant.delete), who did it, which app, what it was done to, how it ended, text to search for, and when (RFC 3339 times; since inclusive, until exclusive). Each event has a summary in plain words, such as "Deployed crewmate", beside its action.

action.description: Actions starting with this, e.g. app.

before.description: The next_before from a previous page, to read further back.

involving.description: Events where this ID is the actor or the target: everything to do with one account.

outcome.description: Only events with this outcome: success, denied or failed.

principal_id.description: Who did it: a user or token ID, or system, reconciler or detection.

principal_kind.description: What kind of actor: user, token, system or anonymous.

q.description: Text found in the action, the actor's name, email or ID, the target's ID, or the app's ID or name.

target_id.description: The ID of the thing it was done to.

target_kind.description: What kind of thing it was done to, e.g. user, role, app.

tools.name: pando_list_audit_archives
tools.description: The months of the audit log past retention, archived and removed from the live log: each month's row count, first and last event, time range, size, SHA-256 digest, and where it is kept. Events in these months are not in pando_list_audit; the archive itself is a gzip download from GET /api/v1/audit/archives/{id}, or `pando audit archives download`.

tools.name: pando_list_audit_sinks
tools.description: The audit sinks: destinations, such as a SIEM's syslog or HTTPS collector, that the audit log is pushed to as it is written. Each with what it sends where (transport, endpoint, format, actions, exclude, and disclosure, the sentence saying what leaves the installation), its last delivery, backlog, last_error and failing_since, why Pando turned it off if it did, and gap_from and gap_to for a range of events it missed. Needs install.audit.read.

tools.name: pando_list_deliveries
tools.description: A subscription's recent deliveries, newest first: each event, whether it arrived, how many attempts it took, and the last error.

tools.name: pando_list_events
tools.description: List the events a subscription can name: each event's name, whether it is about one app or the whole installation, and its data fields.

tools.name: pando_list_hosts
tools.description: The hosts that have joined this installation's cluster: each one's name, roles (control, app), address, version and when it was last heard from. Needs install.cluster.manage.

tools.name: pando_list_join_tokens
tools.description: Every join token, newest first: its roles, how many of its uses are spent, when it expires and whether it was revoked. Never the token itself. Needs install.cluster.manage.

tools.name: pando_list_my_apps
tools.description: The apps you can open — your launcher — with which are favorites, which of your sections each is filed under, and whether you can also manage it (can_manage), and your sections. Favorites first, then filed apps, then the rest, a page at a time: pass `next_cursor` back as `cursor` for the next page. A different list from pando_list_apps, which is the apps you can administer.

cursor.description: The next_cursor from a previous page.

q.description: Only apps whose name or slug contains this.

tools.name: pando_list_notices
tools.description: What an app's Overview asks of somebody: a configuration not yet deployed, variables with no value, a backup that was not taken, a security score below this installation's minimum, the spec's warnings. Each has a stable key, a message, a fingerprint and whether you have ignored it as it reads now.

tools.name: pando_list_notifications
tools.description: Your notifications inbox, newest first, and how many are unread. unread=true lists only those.

unread.description: true to list only unread notifications. Optional.

tools.name: pando_list_notify_adapters
tools.description: List the notification adapters, each with whether it can send: capabilities.authorized, and problem saying why one cannot. One with web_authorization or manual_authorization that is not authorized, such as Slack, needs pando_connect_notify first.

tools.name: pando_list_notify_channels
tools.description: List the channels a subscription to a notification adapter such as Slack can post to: id, name, private. A private Slack channel is listed once Pando is invited to it with /invite @Pando.

q.description: Only channels whose names contain this. Optional.

tools.name: pando_list_role_holders
tools.description: Who holds a role: the groups granted it, then the accounts holding it, each with via — direct, or group for an account holding it only through a group. An app role's holders are those holding it on any app. A page at a time: pass `next_cursor` back as `cursor`. Needs install.view.

cursor.description: The next_cursor from a previous page.

tools.name: pando_list_secrets
tools.description: List which secrets an app has, and where each came from. Never their values.

tools.name: pando_list_source_branches
tools.description: The branches of a repository, read through a source connection.

tools.name: pando_list_source_repositories
tools.description: The repositories a source connection can read, to pick one for pando_create_app rather than guess its URL. Refused for a connection with no API access, such as an SSH key.

query.description: Optional: only repositories whose name contains this.

tools.name: pando_list_sources
tools.description: The installation's source connections: how Pando reads private repositories on GitHub, GitLab, Azure DevOps, Bitbucket, Gitea or any git host. Each has an id, the host and scope it covers, how it signs in, whether it can list repositories, and whether it is authorized; problem says why one cannot be used. A private repository is read with the connection that covers its URL.

tools.name: pando_list_specs
tools.description: List an app's spec revisions, and which one is pinned. The pinned revision is what runs and what the next deploy ships.

tools.name: pando_list_subscriptions
tools.description: List your event subscriptions: what each listens for, where it sends, and whether it is on. app_id narrows to one app. Newest first, a page at a time: pass `next_cursor` back as `cursor` for the next page.

app_id.description: Only subscriptions about this app. Optional.

cursor.description: The next_cursor from a previous page.

tools.name: pando_list_user_apps
tools.description: The apps an account has access to: its role for managing each, directly or through a group, whether it can use each, and whether you can change that (can_manage). By app name, a page at a time: pass `next_cursor` back as `cursor` for the next page.

cursor.description: The next_cursor from a previous page.

tools.name: pando_list_users
tools.description: The accounts on this installation, newest first, a page at a time: pass `next_cursor` back as `cursor` for the next page. Each carries adapter_name — the identity provider it signs in with — and install_roles — every installation role it holds, and whether it holds it directly or through a group (with the group's name, and the identity provider for a synced group) — and install_role_id, the role granted to the account itself. Needs install.view.

cursor.description: The next_cursor from a previous page.

q.description: Only accounts whose username, display name or email contains this.

tools.name: pando_mark_host_lost
tools.description: Say a host is gone and start the standby of each app homed on it. With three or more hosts Pando does this itself when most of them cannot reach the host; with fewer it never does. Refused while the host answers. A failed app is not failed over. Returns the apps started and the ones skipped, with why. Needs install.cluster.manage.

tools.name: pando_mark_notifications_read
tools.description: Mark one of your notifications read, by notification_id, or every one when it is omitted.

notification_id.description: The notification's ID, ntf_…. Omit to mark every one read.

tools.name: pando_pin_spec
tools.description: Pin a spec revision: what the app converges to, and what the next deploy ships. This does not deploy — call pando_deploy after. On an app that has been deployed, pinning changes what it runs, so it needs app.deploy, and a revision whose deploy needs approval is refused: deploy it instead.

revision.description: The revision number, such as "3", or the revision's ID.

tools.name: pando_plan
tools.description: Show what a deploy would do, without doing it. Side-effect free, so it is safe to call after any change to check the change is deployable.

tools.name: pando_plan_upgrade
tools.description: Whether Pando can upgrade itself in place to a version, and if not, every reason with what to change; which versions in between may break something, with their upgrade notes. Starting an upgrade is not offered here: it takes a backup passphrase, and agents do not hold install.upgrade by default.

version.description: The version to upgrade to, such as 0.4.0, from pando_get_updates.

tools.name: pando_poll_source_authorization
tools.description: Ask once whether the person approved a device authorization started with pando_authorize_source: status pending (slow_down asks for slower polling) or authorized.

tools.name: pando_read_audit_stream
tools.description: Read the audit log in commit order, oldest first, one page at a time. Returns events, cursor and caught_up. Pass the cursor back as after to read on from where this page ended; keep it to ask later what has happened since. Without after it starts at the oldest event in the live log; after: "now" starts after the newest. caught_up says there is nothing past the cursor yet. Delivery is at least once: an event can come back again, and its id is the key to drop it by. Needs install.audit.read.

action.description: Optional. Only actions starting with one of these prefixes, such as grant.

after.description: The cursor a previous page returned, or now. Optional.

exclude.description: Optional. Leave out actions starting with one of these prefixes.

format.description: Optional. native (the archive's line format, the default) or ocsf.

limit.description: Optional. How many events, 1 to 1000. Defaults to 500.

tools.name: pando_redeliver
tools.description: Send a delivery again now, with the whole retry schedule ahead of it.

tools.name: pando_reject_deploy
tools.description: Reject a deploy that is waiting for approval. One rejection ends the request, and the deploy does not run. Approval is a person's sign-off, so by default an installation does not let an agent's token reject either.

comment.description: Optional. Why, recorded with the rejection and shown to whoever asked.

deployment_id.description: The deploy's ID, as pando_list_approvals or pando_deploy returned it.

tools.name: pando_remove_app_from_section
tools.description: Move an app out of one of your launcher sections, back to Your apps.

tools.name: pando_remove_host
tools.description: Remove a host from the cluster. Needs install.cluster.manage.

tools.name: pando_remove_registry_credential
tools.description: Remove an image app's registry credential, so its image is pulled anonymously.

tools.name: pando_rename_app
tools.description: Change an app's display name. Its ID and address do not change.

tools.name: pando_rename_group
tools.description: Rename a group made in Pando. A group synced from an identity provider is renamed there. Needs install.users.manage.

tools.name: pando_rename_section
tools.description: Rename one of your launcher sections.

tools.name: pando_rerun_detection
tools.description: Work out again how to run an app, from its source as it is now: after pando_upload_source, after the repository changed, or after setting a registry credential for a private image. Nothing changes until the new proposal is accepted. Then call pando_get_detection with wait_seconds.

tools.name: pando_reset_user_two_factor
tools.description: Remove another local account's two-factor authentication — its authenticator and recovery codes — for someone who has lost both, and sign it out everywhere. They then sign in with their password alone, and set it up again if host policy requires it. Needs install.users.manage and every installation permission that account holds.

tools.name: pando_restart_app
tools.description: Restart an app's workloads in place. Nothing is rebuilt and nothing is re-read — the same version, started again.

tools.name: pando_restore_notice
tools.description: Show one of an app's notices you ignored again.

key.description: The notice's key, as pando_list_notices lists it, such as variables.unset.

tools.name: pando_revise_detection
tools.description: Tell the install's AI adapter what is wrong with the plan from pando_get_detection, in plain words, e.g. "The app serves on port 8080." It checks the repository, changes what it can show, and replies; the reply, what it changed and what Pando refused are the last entry of `detection.conversation`. Needs an AI adapter.

message.description: What is wrong with the plan.

tools.name: pando_revoke_join_token
tools.description: Revoke a join token, so no host can join with it. Needs install.cluster.manage.

token_id.description: The join token's ID, from pando_list_join_tokens.

tools.name: pando_set_address
tools.description: Change where a configured app is reached. Everything left out keeps what the app has, or takes the adapter's default when moving to another adapter. To put the app in another of the adapter's domains (from pando_get_address), give domain: alone it makes <slug>.<domain>, and with a hostname that is a single name such as docs it makes docs.<domain>. This writes a spec revision and does not deploy; the next deploy moves the app, and the old address stops working then. Without confirm: true it changes nothing and the error says what would move where — tell the person before confirming. A mode the adapter does not default to needs app.routing.override.

adapter_ref.description: The routing adapter, such as rte_cloudflare. Optional; the app's current one.

confirm.description: true to make the change. Left out, nothing changes and the reply says what would.

domain.description: With subdomain mode: which of the adapter's domains the hostname is in, such as example.org. Optional; the adapter's base domain.

hostname.description: With subdomain mode: the hostname, such as notes.example.com, or with domain a single name such as notes. Optional.

mode.description: How the app is addressed. Optional.

path_prefix.description: With path mode: the path, such as /team/notes. Optional.

tools.name: pando_set_app_icon
tools.description: Set the image shown on an app's launcher tile. The image is a PNG, JPEG, WebP or GIF file of at most 256 KB, base64-encoded. SVG is not accepted.

tools.name: pando_set_app_idle
tools.description: Set when Pando stops and deletes an app nobody uses. Both are replaced, so pass what pando_get_app_idle returned for the one you are not changing. Each is a number of days, "never", or "default" for the installation's setting. Both count from the last use, so deleting has to come later than stopping. App settings, not spec: nothing is deployed.

delete_days.description: Days without use before Pando deletes the app, "never", or "default".

stop_days.description: Days without use before Pando stops the app, "never", or "default".

tools.name: pando_set_app_limit
tools.description: Set how many apps an account, or each person in a group, may own. A number, 0 for unlimited, or "clear" to remove it. An account's own value applies whatever its groups say; otherwise the most generous group's, then host policy's max_apps_per_user. Lowering it removes nothing. Needs install.users.manage, which host policy keeps from agents unless an administrator allows it.

group_id.description: A group's ID. Give this or user_id.

max_apps.description: A number of apps, 0 for unlimited, or "clear".

user_id.description: An account's ID. Give this or group_id.

tools.name: pando_set_auto_deploy
tools.description: Turn automatic deploys on or off for an app, and choose what deploys: each new commit on a branch (trigger branch_updated, the default; branch empty follows the branch the app was deployed from), or each new release tag (trigger release_tagged; a release is a tag such as v1.2.3, or one matching tag_pattern, such as release-*). Saved as a new configuration that takes effect at the app's next deploy. Refused while the app's deploys need approval.

branch.description: With branch_updated: the branch to follow.

tag_pattern.description: With release_tagged: which tags are releases, such as release-*.

tools.name: pando_set_notification_preference
tools.description: Turn one of Pando's notifications on or off for you on one channel. kind and channel are as pando_get_notification_preferences lists them.

channel.description: The channel's adapter ID, such as ntf_console.

tools.name: pando_set_registry_credential
tools.description: Set the credential an image app's private image is pulled with, replacing any it had. It belongs to the app and is never given to it. Pando never shows it again; pando_get_registry_credential says only which kind is set.

registry_credential.description: The credential. Either kind basic with username and password (a token that can read the image), or kind ecr with access_key_id, secret_access_key and optionally region, for AWS ECR.

access_key_id.description: With ecr: the AWS access key ID.

password.description: With basic: the password or access token.

region.description: With ecr: the region. Optional; read from the registry host.

secret_access_key.description: With ecr: the AWS secret access key.

tools.name: pando_set_secret
tools.description: Set or rotate one of an app's secrets. Needs app.secrets.write. The app gets it only through a `secret_ref` in its spec: when the reply's `read_by_spec` is false, add {"key": ..., "secret_ref": ...} to a workload's env with pando_create_spec. Deploying after rotating one the app reads recreates its workload with the new value.

key.description: The secret's name, such as NTFY_TOPIC.

tools.name: pando_start_app
tools.description: Start an app that was stopped, bringing back the version that was running.

tools.name: pando_stop_app
tools.description: Stop an app without deleting it. Its storage, configuration and address are kept, and it stays stopped until something starts it again.

tools.name: pando_test_subscription
tools.description: Send a test event to one subscription, whatever its filter says, to check its endpoint. Returns the delivery; read it with pando_get_delivery.

tools.name: pando_unassign_ai_function
tools.description: Turn an AI function off by removing the adapter that handles it.

function.description: The AI function, such as search_audit.

tools.name: pando_unfavorite_app
tools.description: Unpin an app from your launcher.

tools.name: pando_update_subscription
tools.description: Change a subscription's events, url, adapter_id, channel or description, or turn it on or off with enabled (true or false).

channel.description: A new channel, for an adapter such as Slack. Optional.

events.description: Comma-separated event names or patterns. Optional.

headers.description: Replace a webhook's headers: one "Name: value" per line. Optional.

method.description: A webhook's HTTP method: POST, PUT or PATCH. Optional.

payload_template.description: A webhook's body as a Go template. Optional.

tools.name: pando_upload_source
tools.description: Send an app's files as its source: a gzipped tar of the app's directory, base64-encoded, at most 256 MB compressed. Paths in the archive are relative to the app's root; leave out .git, node_modules and build output. A single index.html is enough for a static site. Replaces any files sent before. Then call pando_rerun_detection so Pando works out how to run them.
